This Writ Petition Coming On For Orders,
This Day, The Court Made The Fo Llowing :
 Order

On the earlier date of hearing, the learned Addl. Government Advocate submitted that an alternative efficacious remedy is available by way of an appeal before the tribunal under Section 76 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, but this day she fairly submits on the instructions given by the 1 s t respondent, before this Court, that no tribunal yet has been constituted by the State.
Therefore the writ petition is entertained and the following order is passed.
2. Heard the learned counsels appearing for both the parties.

Perused the impugned order which is at Annexure-E.
3.

The brief factual matrix of the case is that the petitioner is a small scale businessman who obtained proper authorization or licence from the Government for the purpose of starting a pure drinking water unit in Belagavi.
Accordingly he has started running the business.
That on 19.9.2016 the respondent No.2 has visited the working unit of the petitioner.
At that time the petitioner was not present.
However the 3rd respondent was present at that time and it is alleged that the petitioner has been running the said unit without ISI certificate and also running the same without proper licence.
The respondent No.2 found, 37 packed water cans and 3 empty water cans in the said unit and he has seized them for the purpose of sending the same for scientific examination to the laboratory.
Accordingly the case has been registered against the petitioner in No.RB/NS/FSSA/CR-01/ 2016-17.

The Additional Deputy Commissioner and the Authorized Officer under the Food and Civil Supplies Act, has conducted the enquiry and passed the impugned order as Premanand S/O Ganapati Kavale vs The Ex-Officio & Additional on 14 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165701703/
2 per Annexure-E imposing penalty of `2,00,000/- on the petitioner directing him to pay the said amount within one month and also directed not to indulge in manufacturing misbranded articles and also directed him to destroy the misbranded articles in his unit.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. The learned counsel for the petitioner drawn attention of this Court that a notice was issued to the petitioner to appear before the respondent No.1 on 10.1.2017 at 11.30 a.m. and subsequently the case has been adjourned and on 7.2.2017 the case was taken up and on that day after hearing both the parties the order has been passed on the same day imposing penalty.

The learned counsel seriously contends that no opportunity has been given to the petitioner to file his objections or to lead any evidence nor the evidence of the said Sri M.S.Bekkeri who has not been subjected to any cross examination.

It is evident from the orders that on 7.2.2017 itself everything has been concluded and on 25.3.2017 and the order has been passed by the respondent No.1.
5.

There is no whisper in the orders passed that any opportunity was given to the petitioner to file his objections and to cross examine Mr.M.S.Bekkeri and as well as to lead his evidence before passing the impugned order.

When the respondent No.1 has taken a drastic decision to impose a huge amount of `2,00,000/- as penalty, it is incumbent upon the officer i.e., respondent No.1 to provide sufficient opportunity to the petitioner so as to counter the allegations made against him.
6. Under the above said circumstances, this Court do not find any reasons to sustain the order passed by the 1 s t respondent, as the same is against to the principles of natural justice.
The impugned order deserves to be quashed.
7. The order dated 25.3.2017 in No.RB/NS/FSSA/CR-01/2016-17 as per Annexure-E, passed by the respondent No.1 is hereby quashed.

The said proceedings are restored on to the file of the Addl.
Deputy Commissioner and Authorized Officer, with a direction that after giving opportunity to the petitioner to file his objections and to cross examine Sri M.S.Bekkeri and also for leading evidence,
thereafter, after hearing the arguments of both the counsels the respondent No.1 has to dispose of the said proceedings in accordance with law.
